es.example: Vamos al grano, no tenemos mucho tiempo.
es.exampleTranslation: Let's get to the point, we don't have much time.

it.literal: to go to the solid part
it.meaning: To get to the heart of the matter.
it.exampleTranslation: Let's cut to the chase: how much does it cost?

bridge.note: Both strip away the husk: Spanish reaches the grain, Italian the sodo (firm core). Both stay polite in professional register — useful meeting phrases.

interference.es_to_it: 'Andare al grano' isn't Italian — the core is il sodo, the firm part.
interference.it_to_es: 'Ir al sodo' means nothing in Spanish. The husk comes off to reach el grano.
